Commentary.Commentary: A completely one-sided affair draws to a close, but these two quality teams promise a far tighter contest next time. The second T20I comes up on Friday, 9th January 2026 at 1.30 pm GMT. Join us ahead of time for the build-up. Until then, cheers!

The captain of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says he was not expecting the dew to settle in, given the cloudy weather, but it eventually did, and he feels the toss proved decisive. Tells that there was grip and turn in the first innings, and he felt that 140-150 would have been a challenging total. Adds that the surface got better in the second innings, and considering how it played, he feels 170 would have been a challenging total. Shares that the team knows what needs to be done heading into the World Cup and they want different players to play their roles, and he wants the team to improve the fielding. He jokes that it is becoming a habit for him to be dismissed on full tosses and that it has become a weakness, given that this is the third time (as per him) it has happened.

Dasun Shanaka, the captain of Sri Lanka, says that in T20 cricket, the toss plays a vital role and setting a target is never easy. He admits they did not get the start they wanted and lost wickets in clusters, an issue the team needs to address. He feels there was a phase where they recovered, but Janith Liyanage's dismissal at that point stalled the momentum. Mentions that they should have scored at least 150 on this surface. Shanaka adds that they need to hunt for more wickets and acknowledges there was a lack of buzz in the field, the kind of energy other teams bring and something they must show, especially at home. He explains that they had a clear bowling plan, using Nuwan Thushara with the new ball to pick up early wickets, but concedes it was simply an off day for the pacer. Dasun says that he is confident that the team will correct these areas going forward.

Plenty of good performers in this match, and Shadab Khan is chosen for the Player of the Match award, as his 2-wicket over is considered decisive by the adjudicators. Shadab Khan thanks the Almighty and says that returning to the international setup is always tough, as you start from zero. He adds that he is very happy. Feels that playing in the BBL helped him gain confidence. Tells that he focused on doing the simple things well. Mentions that the surface helped him and stresses that assessing the conditions is always crucial. Further says that he bowled a little fuller than a good length, with the ball holding up slightly. Shares that it is always a dream to play the World Cup and feels this is just one step as a team. Praises the pace bowlers for setting the tone upfront for him and the rest of the spinners to do their job in the middle phase.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Pakistan ticked plenty of boxes in this outing. Salman Mirza's new ball burst in the Powerplay, Shadab Khan's reassuring return with the ball, Abrar Ahmed's steady rise as a wicket-taker, and the opening stand between Sahibzada Farhan and Saim Ayub all stood out. They barely put a foot wrong, though a couple of dropped catches did sneak in. Something to fine-tune as they move ahead.

Sri Lanka will want to file this away as an off day at the office. The batting misfired badly and apart from a brief moment when Janith Liyanage and Wanindu Hasaranga joined forces, there was no momentum in their batting inning. The bowling also offered little resistance. The surface did have some bite, with uneven bounce on offer, but the Lankan attack lacked the discipline to cash in. Nuwan Thushara bore the brunt in the Powerplay as both Pakistan openers lined him up, feasting on his pace and those off-radar deliveries. With very little to defend, the spinners of Sri Lanka also failed to have any impact.

Easy peasy for Pakistan. A neat and clean outing where they were never stretched. A paltry target was on offer, and it was tucked away inside the Powerplay as they raced to 59 without fuss. A few wickets did fall, but the finish line was never out of sight. Sahibzada Farhan was once again impressive with the bat as he continues to make a name for himself in this format.

Usman Khan hits the winning runs! Flat and short, on middle. Usman goes deep in the crease and pulls it to the left of deep square leg and comes back for the second run. Pakistan win by 6 wickets, with 20 balls to spare and take the lead in the series.

Commentary.Commentary: A flying start for Pakistan. That would have surely settled any nerves. Maheesh Theekshana to continue.
Goes full and outside off, Farhan strokes it down off the bottom half of the bat. It rolls through mid on and they take a run. 19 from this over and Pakistan have raced to 40 in no time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This one sails over the fence as well. It's a great start from Pakistan, making a statement. Sharp delivery, short and on middle at 134 kph, Sahibzada Farhan eases himself on the back foot, brings a horizontal bat down and smokes it over deep backward square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! OUT OF HERE! Yet another slower one attempted, at 117 clicks and this has been handled with authority. Fuller and outside off, Sahibzada Farhan fetches it and towers it behind the bowler's head for a maximum. Lasith Malinga, the fast-bowling consultant, looks worried.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Fullish and on off, taking the pace off, Sahibzada Farhan brings his bat down and pushes it to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it very full and around leg, moving a bit into the batter, Ayub clips it to deep mid-wicket for a single. All looks very easy for Pakistan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nuwan Thushara to Saim Ayub, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Another wrong line. Nuwan Thushara comes from over the wicket and bowls a length ball down the leg side. He is lucky as Saim fails to get any bat behind it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Nuwan Thushara to Saim Ayub, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Stylish! This young man is a very attractive-looking stroke player. Nuwan steams in from 'round the wicket and serves a full ball on middle and leg. Saim Ayub leans forward and across, lifts it off his pads and puts it away to the fence at mid-wicket. Nuwan continues to struggle with his line.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Nuwan Thushara to Saim Ayub, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Will Nuwan Thushara get a second over in his opening burst? The answer is yes. Dasun Shanaka is backing the slingy pacer to make amends after an ordinary first over.

Edgy! Maheesh Theekshana delivers it around leg and this one grips a bit. Sahibzada Farhan closes the face of his bat to work it on the leg side but gets a leading edge. It goes safely to covers. 9 from the second over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fullish and around middle, Saim drives it back and it races past the diving bowler to long off. They take a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Saim Ayub, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Dismissed! This is how Saim Ayub is known to bat. Tossed up, full and outside off, there is enough room available for the batter who exercises his arms. Goes inside-out and hammers it over extra cover for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Saim Ayub, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated and full, on middle, it's knocked down to long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker through the air, around off, at 101 kph, Ayub punches it from the crease, past the cover fielder, and a run is taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Saim Ayub, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Loopy and full, on middle, from 'round the wicket, Saim drives off the front foot to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Saim Ayub, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be spin from the other end in the form of Maheesh Theekshana. He is starting with a slip in place.

FOUR! Consecutive boundaries to close the first over. Nuwan is struggling with his line. Delivers it full and around leg at 136 kph, easy pickings for Sahibzada Farhan. He once again picks it off his pads and flicks it with great timing, towards mid-wicket, for a boundary. 12 from the first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Eased away! Nuwan Thushara once again loses his radar. Serves it full and down the leg side, Farhan picks it off his pads and neatly nudges it down to fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off, Sahibzada Farhan shifts his weight on the back foot and punches it through the line. Finds the cover fielder who makes no mistake this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nuwan Thushara changes his angle for the left-hander. Speeds in from 'round the wicket and spears in a yorker on middle. Saim Ayub does well to bring his bat down in time. He digs it out to mid-wicket and crosses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Nuwan Thushara to Saim Ayub, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nuwan gets his line right and delivers a full ball outside off. A hint of movement. Farhan drives away from his body, towards covers, where the fielder fumbles and parries it towards mid off. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nuwan Thushara begins with a delivery that's not on the mark. Full and on the pads, Sahibzada Farhan flicks it easily through mid-wicket and opens his account with a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Nuwan Thushara to Sahibzada Farhan, 2 runs.
